purpose: Each path below is an independent chain of artifacts that, when followed, leads a team from an observable anomaly to the hidden truth of that thread. Teams may find one, two or all three paths. The T10 path is the meta-path that connects the utility attack back to the STATE-X/KESTREL network documented in the Rafael base world.

paths.name: Grid intrusion

join_path.observation: 32,000 customers in northwest and central Corpus Christi experienced outages lasting 21+ days. The affected areas had measured peak gusts of 50–65 mph during Rafael — a band that produced <36-hour outages in comparable areas during hurricanes Harvey and Harvey-analog scenarios in ERCOT historical records.
join_path.significance: Mismatch between storm severity and restoration duration is the initial anomaly that flags possible non-storm cause.

join_path.artifact: GW-SYS-RTU-01 relay configuration dump vs. D-30 commissioning test report
join_path.observation: Current relay 27-UV threshold = 0.94 pu. Commissioning report (D-30) = 0.88 pu. No change order exists for the modification. The modification timestamp in the RTU config file = D-3 17:04Z.
join_path.significance: Proves the relay was deliberately set to a hair-trigger threshold before the storm, not damaged by it. D-3 timestamp predates any storm-related work.

join_path.artifact: GW-SYS-SCADA-01 operator-command log, D+7 and D+10
join_path.observation: Breaker-OPEN commands were sent to GW-FAC-SUB-02 CB-7 (D+7 14:28Z) and GW-FAC-SUB-03 CB-12 (D+10 19:43Z) from workstation GW-WS-OPS-02. No operator was logged in to that workstation at either time (confirmed by physical access badge log and SCADA console session table).
join_path.significance: Commands were sent remotely via the jump host, not by any CBPWA operator. Proves active adversary presence during the restoration phase.

join_path.observation: 14 authenticated sessions from IP blocks outside Texas, all using credential GW-ENG-VELA, spanning D-7 to D+16. Session at D+7 14:27–14:33Z and D+10 19:40–19:50Z coincide exactly with the unauthorized SCADA commands.
join_path.significance: Ties the remote actor (via stolen credential GW-ENG-VELA) to both the relay pre-staging and the active D+7/D+10 trips. Confirms external actor, not insider.

paths.answer: STATE-X/KESTREL used a stolen CBPWA engineer credential to pre-modify relay trip thresholds before the hurricane (causing premature trip at D0) and to issue remote breaker-open commands at D+7 and D+10 during the restoration effort, extending power outages for 32,000 customers by approximately 3 weeks beyond the storm-only baseline.

paths.name: Water SCADA manipulation

join_path.artifact: City boil water notice + field report GW-FR-0912
join_path.observation: Boil water notice for Districts 3–4 issued D+12. Field report logs Zone 4 pressure at 16–18 psi at D+12 15:44Z. The 20 psi regulatory threshold had been breached for at least 3 days before detection.
join_path.significance: Establishes the effect and that it went undetected for days — suggesting a monitoring failure, not just storm damage.

join_path.observation: ZONE4-LOW-PRES alarm is listed as suppressed since D-3 17:09Z. No work order authorized this suppression. The suppression was added in the same SCADA session that modified the relay settings.
join_path.significance: Explains why the pressure drop went unalarmed for 3 days. The suppression was an adversary action, not a maintenance configuration. The same session authoring both the relay change and the alarm suppression is a critical cross-thread tie.

join_path.artifact: Meridian historian: FAC-UTL-01-P3-SET-PSI tag and motor amperage log
join_path.observation: P3-SET-PSI drops from 85 to 68 at D+9 02:04Z under user 'GW-ENG-VELA'. Motor amperage drops 11 A at the same time — consistent with reduced load, inconsistent with any storm or pipe damage (pipe damage would cause flow, not setpoint, change).
join_path.significance: Proves the pressure drop was caused by a deliberate setpoint change, not hurricane-damaged infrastructure. The GW-ENG-VELA credential links this to the grid-intrusion sessions.

join_path.observation: GW-FAC-WTR-03-BSTR-SET-PSI changed from 72 to 54 psi at D+9 02:08Z — 4 minutes after the FAC-UTL-01 setpoint change. Same user, same session. This reduced upstream pipeline flow, compounding the shortage at FAC-UTL-01.
join_path.significance: Shows the adversary modified both the treatment plant and the upstream source pipeline in the same session — a coordinated water-supply reduction, not a single-point failure.

paths.answer: Using stolen CBPWA credentials, STATE-X/KESTREL pre-suppressed the Zone 4 low-pressure alarm (D-3) and then simultaneously lowered treatment plant pump P-3 and upstream booster station setpoints on D+9, reducing Zone 4 water pressure to 14 psi. The alarm suppression masked the problem for 3 days, triggering a 30-day boil water notice for 48,000 residents.

paths.name: Hiding in the storm

join_path.artifact: Outage-duration map vs. storm-track wind-field contours
join_path.observation: GIS overlay of ERCOT outage-duration map against NOAA/NWS H*Wind modeled peak gust contours shows that the two longest-outage clusters (northwest and central Corpus Christi) fall in the 50–65 mph gust band. Historical restoration data for ERCOT shows this gust band produces <36-hour outages. The affected clusters were still out at D+21.
join_path.significance: Storm footprint cannot explain the outage duration. Something else is holding up restoration.

join_path.observation: The relay threshold modifications and alarm suppression were written at D-3 17:04–17:09Z, during the storm-preparation change freeze. The storm made landfall at D0 06:00Z. The adversary staged more than 3 days before first impact — the modifications could not have been caused by the storm.
join_path.significance: Temporal impossibility rules out storm as a cause of the relay and alarm changes. This is the strongest single artifact for proving deliberate action.

join_path.artifact: GW-SYS-JMP-01 session log + KESTREL IOC set (TLP:RED, shared with TCC)
join_path.observation: Two of the 14 VPN session source IPs (45.141.x.x and 185.220.x.x) appear in a classified indicator set for the KESTREL threat cluster shared with the Texas Cyber Command under TLP:RED. The same IP blocks were observed in the Rafael T6 tanker-valve cyber thread and T7 covert port attack communications.
join_path.significance: Links the utility intrusion to the STATE-X/KESTREL network that orchestrated the tanker-valve attack (T6) and the covert military action at the port (T7). All three operations — hurricane exploitation, grid/water attack, and port disruption — share adversary infrastructure, pointing to a coordinated multi-vector STATE-X campaign timed to Hurricane Rafael.

paths.answer: STATE-X deliberately timed the utility intrusion to Hurricane Rafael to use the storm as camouflage. The relay modifications predate the storm (D-3), the breaker-open commands mimicked storm switching, and the pressure drop was masked by pre-staged alarm suppression. The mismatch between storm intensity and outage duration, the pre-storm modification timestamps, and KESTREL infrastructure reuse — shared with the Rafael T6/T7 covert operations — collectively prove this was a coordinated multi-thread STATE-X campaign, not a cascade of storm effects.
